## Status and source

**OPEN — the robot is not yet physically accepted.** This issue is the single live implementation/completion plan and remaining-work checklist. `plan.md` points here; it is not a second task list. Coordinator: Nicholas. Subsystem owners verify their own calibration, data layouts and results.

Software baseline: main `565bae7e95668d172fe4b632a14209afc4b4b548` (PRs #139, #140 and #141). The three-application-task refactor, most feature code and software regressions are implemented. INT-49 records full host/dashboard/CLI/HTTP passes and all four firmware builds against integrated source `545a6a3`; its application/build/test sources match this main baseline. Those are **host/build results**, not firmware execution, calibrated limits or physical passes.

Use the [requirements and pending decisions](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/docs/project-specs.md), [architecture/contracts](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/docs/architecture.md), [hardware/team guide](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/docs/team.md), [ordered physical procedures](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/testing/mission-readiness.md), [test-recording rules](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/testing/README.md#run-and-record), and [video index](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/blob/main/docs/week13-plan.md#video-index). Owning guides retain requirements, numeric limits and measurements; this issue owns work order and completion status. The old plan's stages 0–9 are summarized below through completed software and the remaining sequence; old stage numbers in historical evidence keep their meaning.

## Completed software

These checkmarks mean **implemented and software-verified**, not physically accepted. Do not rebuild these refactors solely because their old issues had unchecked boxes.

- [x] Shared time/wrap helpers, GPIO IRQ dispatcher, configuration/static assertions, packed data accessors and kernel-free host runner.
- [x] Motion-only motor output, independent local GP21/stop/expiry checks, startup/TEST inhibition and serviced-brake reset ordering; no separate Safety task.
- [x] Mission extracted into `app_program/mission/`; bounded line/barcode/sonar/servo steps; seven repeating states and local-start prerequisites.
- [x] Core-0 I/O steps Terrain/Reporting; coherent acquisition/progress ages, cross-core event synchronization, mapping installed by Mission before ACK; kernel WiFi/USB stay on their existing core.
- [x] Wheel/line controllers, signed encoder actions, barcode A–Z in both print orientations, enable-time quiet-zone reference, next-junction consumption and outgoing-line confirmation.
- [x] Stationary bounded line-recovery pivots/alignment, hump slowdown/height/count/maximum with encounter quality rejection, fixed-storage median/qualified-edge scan helpers and bounded bypass helpers.
- [x] Binary schema-v2 codec/laptop tooling, rejected-ACK failure status, malformed telemetry rejection, and stale RX discard across connection loss.
- [x] Minimum-bit conversions and historical target size/wire evidence; current integration software checks through INT-49 preserved.

**Current limits:** physical bypass is disabled (`MISSION_BYPASS_RELEASED=0`). Recovery is enabled for the current trial; its geometry/gains/timing remain provisional. Stall detection code exists but the trial configuration disables it (`MOTION_STALL_GUARD_ENABLED=0`). `APP_PHYSICAL_RELEASE=0` is not a global motor-inhibit gate. No enabled application reset watchdog is established by the TIMER tick setup. Record actual build settings for every trial.

## Accepted behavior and constraints

- Three application tasks: Motion and Mission on core 1, bounded I/O on core 0; five subsystem modules remain. Kernel WiFi/USB tasks are additional RTOS tasks.
- Only Motion writes motor outputs. Mission chooses movement, mapping installation and local reset. Networking reports/transports requests; it cannot directly start, stop or drive. The documented junction-testing exception lets Mission accept one next-junction direction request.
- GP21 stops; after cause clearance and serviced braking, an eligible GP21 release returns READY without movement. A separate fresh GP20 starts. Required IR/Motion evidence, installed mapping and WiFi/MQTT gate a normal start. Ordinary IMU failure after a bounded startup attempt is flagged/report-only; network loss during a healthy run is report-only.
- Barcode actions occur once at a detected junction and follow the outgoing route; no turn-then-undo, fixed 25 mm advance, automatic COMPLETE or finish marker. Healthy operation loops; GP21 or a stopping guard ends movement. Retired MR-34 is not reused; use MR-40.
- Recovery follows the current stationary wider-pivot decision, not the superseded moving +/-70-degree plan. Hump results persist over accepted starts/stops until reboot. The lower-ramp target is <=30 mm; no invented height-error tolerance.
- Keep micro T-Kernel, C/Pico SDK, current wiring/core ownership, minimum-bit contracts and binary schema. No generic event bus, new scheduler, route planner or watchdog framework is authorized by this cleanup.
- Preserve historical IDs, failures and evidence. Record the exact source commit/profile/image checksum, tester/date, wiring, power and calibration. Keep one power source at a time. Any measured constant change is separately committed, rebuilt and followed by affected reruns.

## Stage 0: Decisions and final test setup

Resolve these before their dependent PASS/release decisions; electrical/boot work can proceed once its own prerequisites are met.

- [ ] Record/locate each owner's fault-byte confirmation from #113/#28, and only then remove provisional approval markers/reconcile affected firmware, docs and decoder. Code agreement is not owner sign-off.
- [ ] Agree missing acceptance limits in D01–D15 for barcode/line sensing, geometry, speed/turn/stall/recovery, height/width errors, stopping, uncertainty, timing, stack and power margins. D11/D16 are settled; preserve the D12 straight-course assumption unless new course evidence changes it. No finish-marker requirement is added.
- [ ] Agree/calibrate the final stall-guard release configuration; a disabled-guard trial cannot count as the MR-25 stall-protection pass.
- [ ] Resolve D15 watchdog policy, enabled state and output behavior. Perform SYS-06 reset injection only if that policy is implemented and the required safe setup exists; a tick divider is not watchdog protection. Record any approved deferral explicitly rather than claiming a pass.
- [ ] Prepare the measured track, issued/reference barcodes, <=30 mm ramps, 100–200 mm obstacles, measurement tools, trace capture, subscriber capture and camera/scope setup.
- [ ] Select the final firmware source/profile and record image checksum, operator/date, wiring, power and initial constants. Keep all unmeasured limits in the pending-decisions register.
- [ ] Review the remaining known upstream build warning: fix or explicitly justify it in final build evidence; no clean-warning claim from a log that still contains it.
- [x] Repository tracking/doc alignment and a source-current completion manifest are merged in [PR #142](https://github.com/shauniee/Autonomous-Robotic-Car/pull/142), main `b398126`. INT-50 verifies local links, unchanged firmware/evidence and current BLOCKED (exit 1). The physical/approval/release work below remains outstanding.

## Stage 1: Electrical release, boot and local control

- [ ] **MR-01..05 / T01:** continuity against the pin map, Grove 6 GP26 disconnect, GP28 battery jumper, measured Echo HIGH <=3.3 V before connection, power polarity and loaded 3V3/VSYS. Record values/limits and brownout observations; the user's wiring/electrical confirmation is not new measurement evidence.
- [ ] **MR-06..07 / T02:** capture actual TEST self-test output with motors inhibited; normal boot inhibition, held buttons, cause-present reset refusal, eligible GP21-release reset and separate fresh GP20 start. Reset must not replay an old command.
- [ ] **MR-09..11 / T12:** refuse unmapped/unready IR/Motion/offline starts; install mapping while stopped and reject it while moving; reboot clears mapping. Missing IMU must show bounded calibration failure and permit readiness once the required inputs qualify.
- [ ] **T02 / D08:** GP21 during FOLLOW, encoder turn/distance, scan, bypass and recovery; measure output-brake latency separately from physical stopping time/distance and stationarity. Do not infer equivalence from host tests.

## Stage 2: Sensor and Motion calibration

- [ ] **MR-12..13 / D01/D04:** mounted raw IR black/white, contrast/noise and lighting range, calibration cues, barcode black polarity, sensor height/spacing and issued-print scale/quiet-zone/rearm values.
- [ ] **MR-14..15 / D03:** three hand-turned forward revolutions per wheel, counts/signs, wrapping consumers, fault detection/clearance and maximum tested encoder edge rate. Do not select polarity from a source diff.
- [ ] **MR-16 / T06:** mounted stationary IMU calibration and fresh/pending/failure ages; axes and nose-up pitch, impact latch/clear ordering. Save labelled stationary, acceleration, braking, turning, climb/descent and impact traces; no gyro-data claim.
- [ ] **MR-17..18 / T08 / D05:** measured sonar error at 100/250/500/1000 mm, no/late/out-of-range echoes and different surfaces/angles; repeat timing, centre/endpoints, slow slew and settled acquisition without servo stall. Unknown range is not clear space or a universal stop.
- [ ] **MR-19..20 / D03:** physical motor-forward polarity, measured wheel diameter/track/wheelbase and encoder-to-distance scaling, full swept vehicle envelope.
- [ ] **MR-21..23 / D07:** 1 m drives five times; left/right 90-degree and 180-degree turns five times each, repeated with one wheel raised on a hump; record lateral/distance/angle errors and wheel PID/line tuning against agreed limits.
- [ ] **MR-24..25 / T05:** physical stopping distance, guard-enabled stall response, cause-clear reset, discrete action completion/timeout and obstacle cancellation; record exact image and guard settings.

## Stage 3: Barcode and junction acceptance

- [ ] **MR-26 / S3-P01 / T03:** three line-follow laps under two lighting conditions, curves and broad-black qualification, after wheel/line tuning.
- [ ] **MR-27 / T04:** issued barcodes in both print orientations at operating speed, including the first print after enabling; same letter/action mapping, known widths/quiet zones and encoder wrap. Test unmapped, malformed, partial, duplicate and overflow encounters; reject rather than guess/replay.
- [ ] **MR-28 / T04/T05:** fresh runtime mapping without rebuild; all four actions once at variable-distance cross junctions; requested stationary U-turn pause, outgoing-line confirmation, no-command straight crossing and repeat visits. Record mounting/print-to-junction/turn-centre offsets; no fixed-distance advance requirement.
- [ ] **MR-32 / T11:** healthy white/white loss uses bounded qualification, stationary sweep and alignment at the current agreed limits; interrupt search, place an obstacle and freeze/fail IR separately. Require bounded return to intended-line tracking or stop; stale acquisition cannot extend blind travel.
- [ ] Verify stop/reset cancels pending movement but retains valid line calibration, installed mapping and retained display context; installing a new mapping while stopped starts a fresh pending-action context.

## Stage 4: Terrain and hump acceptance

- [ ] **MR-29 / T07 / D06:** measure the lower practice ramp plus one lower and one near 30 mm reference (all <=30 mm); save dimensions, tool/resolution, profiles/photos and raised-wheel orientation.
- [ ] Verify a <=30 mm single-wheel ramp crosses the climb/descent thresholds on the mounted robot; inspect pitch/roll, axes, filter delay, missed descent/premature FLAT and false impact behavior. No nominal-distance substitution for missing encoder evidence.
- [ ] Validate half normal tracking speed during a fresh valid encounter, steady measurement and restoration at confirmed end/descent. Test acceleration/braking/slip/turning and incomplete windows; rejected quality must not produce a valid height/count or overwrite a valid maximum.
- [ ] Calibrate the height method/factor against the references; agree error tolerance and tested speed range, cutoff/crest/quality thresholds in D06. Keep the reported scale unless measurements justify a reviewed change.
- [ ] With final constants, perform three passes per reference (at least nine), recording actual/reported height, signed error, speed, wheel, detector state and count/event increment. Larger then smaller humps retain the greatest valid maximum. Stop/new start retain completed results until reboot.

## Stage 5: Obstacle profiling and bypass release

- [ ] **MR-30..31 / T08..T10 / D02/D03/D05/D10:** calibrate sonar/servo/model settings and stationary repeated/median scans; demonstrate moving-scan rejection, qualified adjacent-ray edges/hysteresis, optional background handling, widths/depths and repeatable uncertainty for 100–200 mm obstacles. Planning bounds must not be displayed as measured widths.
- [ ] Measure the full chassis/turning envelope, trigger/stopping margin, side gaps and supported forward/side coverage at the actual servo limits. Restore-centre acquisition must be genuinely fresh; no lost Echo means rear clearance and no side reading refreshes front clearance.
- [ ] Validate both-side selection, departure/parallel leg, qualified rear edge plus full-car clearance, measured depth, original-line return/alignment and repeated tracking. Reject wrong crossings, a second obstacle, unknown evidence, both sides blocked, exhausted retry/travel/deadline and unsupported reverse.
- [ ] Resolve/calibrate any remaining coverage/rear-edge/original-line implementation gaps identified by those trials; rerun affected software/build/physical checks. Keep bypass release inhibited until its envelope/coverage policy supports acceptance; explicitly authorize and record the release change after qualification.
- [ ] No curved-course or blind reverse claim. Additional scan positions or chassis compensation are optional after a supported basic bypass, not a new routing framework.

## Stage 6: Network, fault and real-time acceptance

- [ ] **MR-08 / T12:** Pico-originated telemetry/snapshots at the documented cadence; verify units/validity, counts, derived speed/direction, mission/motion/line states, mapped flag, six fault bytes, hump results, barcode/action, dimensions and event order/time/position against the robot.
- [ ] **MR-33 / T13:** interrupt WiFi/broker under acquisition/scan/report load and reconnect; healthy local control and GP21 continue, faults report, current data resumes and stale commands never replay. Reject prohibited/malformed remote commands; mapping ACK means installed.
- [ ] **T14:** stale/frozen producers, stalled Mission updates, expired commands, encoder/stall/impact faults and full capture/navigation/diagnostic buffers; bounded processing and documented stop behavior independent of congestion. Record drops/occupancy and unsupported cases.
- [ ] **MR-39 / S3-M02 / T15 / D13:** define a bounded measurement/capture method for the final Motion/Mission/I/O tasks; adapt useful instrumentation from superseded PR #115 if appropriate. Do not restore its obsolete two-task names, unconditional console output or arbitrary historical 10 ms pass threshold.
- [ ] Measure TEST and normal motor-load releases/WCET/jitter/missed deadlines, line-to-output latency, IMU/sample ages under timeout/reconnect, GPIO IRQ edge rate/service time, brake response, queue/ring high-water marks and stack/heap/peak-RAM margins against agreed D13 limits. Slow MQTT alone cannot establish short deadlines.

## Stage 7: Mixed mission and submission

- [ ] **MR-35:** fresh boot, bounded IMU outcome then IR calibration, connect, unfamiliar-letter mapping, fresh local start; measure boot-to-start time and refusal of missing required prerequisites.
- [ ] **MR-36..37 / MR-40 / T16:** three consecutive successful observation sessions on unchanged firmware/constants with variable feature order, both barcode orientations/all junction actions, <=30 mm humps and accepted obstacles/bypass. Repeat junctions with/without instructions, interrupt network, end with GP21 and require deliberate reset/new start. A corrective code/constant change restarts the three-session sequence; no automatic finish marker.
- [ ] **MR-38:** reconstruct route/encounter order from saved event/monitor output and counts, and compare against observed video; record uncertainty, bypass success/time, interventions and failures.
- [ ] Refresh final source-pinned text/data/bss, target `sizeof`/linked persistent objects, inter-task copies, exact schema lengths (including junction-test extension), boundary regressions and four build profiles. Static allocation is not measured live margin; a before/after comparison is not required by the later course clarification.
- [ ] Commit append-only results, traces, failures/reruns and image hashes; index actual unlisted video links with test ID/commit and matching TEST_LOG rows. Do not commit credentials, firmware binaries or videos. Placeholder video rows are not evidence.
- [ ] Final all-stage completion audit matches the accepted source and evidence, with every requirement/accepted decision covered or an explicit approved scope decision. No remaining mission-blocking failure or unqualified release.

## Completion rule

Keep this issue **open** until all applicable remaining items have actual, linked acceptance evidence on the accepted source, owner confirmations/limits are recorded, and the three unchanged-image sessions pass. Mark physical boxes only from recorded measurements, never from code inspection, a build or a host test. Unsupported/unavailable work stays unchecked unless an explicit approved scope decision is linked. Current code presence is not a declaration that bypass or full mission readiness works.

## Consolidated history

Replaces the live tracking in #129–#133 and the old physical-readiness PR #115; #117's original history is retained. Completed software is on main. Unfinished calibration/physical/submission work from cleanup-closed #28, #30, #32, #38, #40, #47, #55, #59–#62, #113 and #114 is captured above. #123's <=30 mm ramp acceptance and #124's actual video indexing are also retained. Historical issue bodies/comments, test IDs, failed builds and results remain accessible; consolidation does not retroactively mark them passed.

The earlier plan at main `565bae7` remains in Git history. Its software stages are implemented as summarized above; its remaining acceptance is this sequence. Subsystem ownership and task/contracts remain in their owning guides, not duplicated mutable requirements here.
title: Robot completion plan and remaining acceptance
